calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Stars
calls.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Stars’ power play is one of the league’s best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates at least their usual 8.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Dallas 3rd for power play (8.7 expected goals per 60) · San Jose 24th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Dallas’s power play created 10.7 expected goals per 60 in 6:00 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.7, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: Expect a grind
calls.body: San Jose plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does Dallas. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than 75.6 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): San Jose 26th (79.5), Dallas 32nd (75.6)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 60.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the slower team’s usual 75.6 and a league average of 81.9.

DAL.head: We gave Dallas a 62% chance, and Dallas delivered.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 38% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Dallas leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Dallas’s bottom-six forwards played 45% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 40% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

surprises.head: Dallas buried San Jose in shots
surprises.body: Dallas took 70% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Dallas would expect about 53%. A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

story.head: Oettinger shuts out the Sharks
paras: Miro Heiskanen opened the scoring late in the first. Five different Stars scored. Jake Oettinger stopped all 13 shots.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Stars win nine in ten. By our Swing measure, Jason Robertson had the best night of anyone.

items.text: Both of the preview’s calls held.
